authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Diaz-Londono C.; Yilmaz Y.E.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems 26(2):2410-2421 (online Dec 2024)
problem: Open Gym simulator for EV smart charging/V2G at CPO level (chargers grouped under transformers); case studies PST (20 chargers) and V2G profit max with loads (10 bidirectional chargers)
method: Simulator + benchmark of RL (SB3: A2C, ARS, SAC, DDPG, TD3, TQC, PPO, TRPO), heuristics, MPC and Gurobi oracle
architecture: n/a (environment); flat Box action of size = number of EVSE ports, per-port in [0,1] (G2V) or [-1,1] (V2G) scaled to charger max current; flat observation whose length grows with #ports
constraint_handling: other:env clips EVSE/BMS current; transformer overload NOT blocked (only measured) + penalty in reward
environment_or_data: EV2Gym; ElaadNL arrivals/departures/energy, Pecan Street loads, Renewables.ninja PV, ENTSO-E prices; 15-min steps (configurable), ~85-112 steps/episode
baselines: AFAP, ALAP, Round Robin; real-time MPC (eMPC/OCMF in code); Gurobi optimal (perfect information)
key_results: PST 20 chargers (100 runs): energy-tracking error Optimal 46+-14 kWh, RR 57+-16, AFAP 313+-59, RL 213-295 kWh; V2G 10 chargers: TD3 profit 31.1 EUR but user satisfaction 38%, Optimal 100% satisfaction
limitations: Fixed-size flat state/action; RL baselines reach very low user satisfaction; no power flow in paper version; departure energy hard only in MIP (in code v2.0.0 the Gurobi profit-max oracle uses a quadratic satisfaction penalty and hard transformer limit)
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.01849 (WebFetch) + EV2Gym 2.0.0 source from PyPI (MIT license)

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Robu V.; Salazar E.M.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
problem: CPO-level PST (and V2G profit) over 25/100/500/1000 charge points grouped by transformers
method: EV-GNN: end-to-end GNN actor/critic combined with SAC/TD3 (also multi-discrete TD3); branch pruning of empty chargers
architecture: Heterogeneous graph (EV, charger, transformer, CPO nodes), type-specific MLP encoders + GCN layers; per-node action output; critic with mean pooling
baselines: AFAP, Round Robin, MPC/oracle (Gurobi), A2C, DDPG, TRPO, TQC, SAC, TD3, PPO variants, FX-GNN
key_results: 1000 CPs: SAC EV-GNN 98.7% user satisfaction, 11 MWh tracking error vs classic SAC 95.9%/17 MWh; actor ~256k vs ~2.8M parameters
limitations: Separate model trained per scale (no train-small/test-large zero-shot in preprint); no transformer/departure constraint enforcement; authors list safe RL as future work; 'prove' in abstract is empirical
evidence_source: Research Square preprint rs-5504138 v1 PDF (WebFetch); published abstract via OpenAlex

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Panda N.K.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
problem: CPO V2G smart charging (25 chargers main; 250 chargers scaled) with aggregate power limit and departure energy targets
method: GNN-DT: offline Decision Transformer conditioned on return-to-go, trained on random/round-robin/optimal trajectories
architecture: GCN state/action embedders + GPT-2 causal transformer (3 layers, 4 heads); per-node action by dot product of output token with node embedding; masking of absent EVs
baselines: DT, Q-DT, SAC, DDPG, TD3, TRPO, PPO, TQC, BaU round robin, CAFAP, offline optimal
key_results: 25 chargers: user satisfaction 99.3%, power violation 21.7+-22.8 (optimal 2.0+-4.6, BaU 10.5); journal abstract: rewards within 5% of oracle; zero-shot 25->5/50/75/100 chargers degrades with size but stays above BaU
limitations: Imitation of offline data; constraints only through reward/data quality; violations higher than BaU; zero-shot only up to 100 chargers; 250-charger case retrained
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01778 (arXiv preprint, WebFetch); journal abstract via OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Oliehoek F.A.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
problem: Network-level EV charging with voltage limits: IEEE 34-bus with 150 V2G chargers; IEEE 123-bus with 500 chargers
method: PI-TD3: TD3 with actor gradients back-propagated through K-step rollouts of a differentiable power-flow and SoC model
architecture: Not specified in preprint; flat state whose length grows with fleet/network size
environment_or_data: EV2Gym + RL-ADN power flow; ElaadNL-based arrivals; 15-min steps, 300-step episodes
baselines: CAFAP, no charging, SAC, PPO, TD3, oracle MPC (perfect information)
key_results: 34-bus: user satisfaction 95.6+-3.6% vs TD3 90.2% and oracle MPC 99.9%; voltage violations per bus 104.2 vs TD3 127.8 and MPC 98.7
limitations: Voltage and departure energy only as soft penalties; no transfer across fleet sizes/topologies; architecture unreported

authors: Wang X.; Nimalsiri N.I.; Xia Y.; Wang P.; Halgamuge S.K.
problem: Voltage-safe EV charging in nested CRE21 Australian distribution networks: 1-32 transformers, 200-3,218 EVs (one charger per EV), hourly decisions
method: Parameter-shared heterogeneous-graph SAC with PID-Lagrangian voltage cost + safety filter (learned graph residual risk sets intervention authority, LinDistFlow projection via truncated POCS sets direction)
architecture: Heterogeneous bus/EV graph, edge-aware message passing with GraphGPS-style global token and EV cross-attention; 383,702 parameters at all scales
environment_or_data: pandapower AC power flow; Ausgrid demand/PV, AEMO prices, VISTA mobility; 240 train / 100 eval days
baselines: ISAC, centralized SAC, MADDPG, perfect-information LP (PI-LP); filter ablations
key_results: Bus-step voltage violations 3.93-7.74% (no filter) -> 0.52-3.44%; departure success 99.06-100%; zero-shot 8->16/32 transformers (2,239/3,218 EVs): 0.57-0.75% violations, >=99.99% departure success
limitations: Explicitly no pointwise feasibility claim; Proposition 1 only gives sign of LinDistFlow correction; departure energy via reward + heuristic service map; transformer loading not constrained

authors: Zhang A.; Liu C.; Makantasis K.; Chen X.; Ward T.E.; Cheng L.
problem: Single charging station with PV and energy storage system; EV charging scheduling
method: DRL with dual-layer safety modules (decision-level safety layer detects and replaces unsafe actions) + reward shaping to align raw and safe actions
environment_or_data: Simulation of a charging station with renewables and ESS
key_results: Abstract: satisfies user demand, reduces operating cost and complies with safety constraints during training and deployment (no numbers in abstract)
limitations: Full text not accessible (Wiley blocked); no evidence of variable-N policy or formal proof in abstract

authors: Wu T.; Scaglione A.; Surani A.-P.; Arnold D.; Peisert S.
problem: Aggregate EV charging demand (state counts by remaining charge time/slack) co-optimised with DC-OPF; IEEE 14-bus with one EV station
method: Constrained TD3 with primal-dual (augmented Lagrangian) updates; per-bus projection of predicted EV demand onto feasible transitions at execution
environment_or_data: Texas demand data + scaled wind; non-stationary Poisson arrivals
baselines: Oracle optimisation with perfect information, unconstrained DRL, no demand response
key_results: 100% feasible actions vs 83.87% for unconstrained DRL; normalized MAE to oracle ~1.9%; fuel cost -31.35% vs no EV demand response
limitations: Single small system; aggregate (not per-charger) model; no transformer limit; DC power flow; convergence proof deferred to earlier work

authors: Christensen K.; Jorgensen B.N.; Ma Z.G.
problem: Residential LV feeder (Strib, Denmark), 126 households all with EVs under a 400 kVA transformer; one-year minute-resolution simulation
method: Rule-based aggregator: shifts highest-laxity EVs out of overload hours to cheapest feasible slots (no learning)
environment_or_data: Danish 2019 hourly consumption, DK1 2024 spot prices + ToU tariff, Danish EV registrations
key_results: Abstract: overloads completely eliminated; aggregator compensation under DKK 6000/year, far below transformer reinforcement cost
limitations: Not RL; algorithm repeats 'until resolved or shifting is impossible' so no guarantee; full participation and perfect forecasts assumed
evidence_source: https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/17/9/3847 (WebFetch; Sec.1-4.6 read, results section not parsed)

authors: Ferragut A.; Narbondo L.; Paganini F.
problem: EV parking facility with capacity C simultaneous chargers; deadlines (sojourn times) reported with error
method: Mean-field (fluid) analysis of EDF and LLF under uncertain deadlines; curtailed variants for incentive compatibility
key_results: Mean attained service in overload independent of uncertainty; under-reporting deadlines is rewarded unless policies are curtailed (Propositions 1-6)
limitations: Mean-field limit, overload regime, exponential/uniform closed forms; no learning, no transformer model beyond capacity C

authors: Rossi F.; Diaz-Londono C.; Li Y.; Zou C.; Gruosso G.
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology
problem: EV charging/discharging scheduling at charging stations on a benchmark grid, mitigating overloads at chosen grid nodes
method: Pre-trained RL scheduler with grid simulation in the loop
environment_or_data: Benchmark distribution grid with realistic station utilisation scenarios
key_results: Qualitative: robust and efficient scheduling (no numbers in abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; objective combines cost, ancillary-service reward and overload mitigation (soft)
evidence_source: Semantic Scholar abstract (IEEE page not renderable)

authors: Yilmaz Y.E.; Orfanoudakis S.; Vergara P.P.
problem: CPO power-setpoint tracking for a commercial parking lot
method: DDPG with action/state design encoding power constraints
architecture: Not stated in abstract (flat MLP implied)
key_results: Lower PST error than uncontrolled charging (qualitative)
limitations: Abstract only; single lot size

authors: Guo J.; Li T.; Xu W.
venue: Proc. 5th Int. Conf. Automation Control, Algorithm and Intelligent Bionics (ACAIB)
problem: V2G charging stations under a single power transformer
method: HSCA-MARL: per-station actor-critic agents + global critic quantifying system risk + contribution-driven value transfer
architecture: Local actor-critic per station, global critic
key_results: Better convergence, global return and lower variance of individual return (qualitative)
limitations: Abstract only; transformer constraint handled only through learned global risk/reward

authors: Demirel G.; Grafenhorst S.; Ohm J.; Schafer B.; Forderer K.; Hagenmeyer V.
problem: Low-voltage grid flexibility dispatch (household with PV, battery, EV, heat pump; 7-PCC feeder) in eGridLVGym
method: Eight single-objective RL algorithms + grid-code shielding + MORL (CAPQL)
baselines: Rule-based controller; A2C, DDPG, PPO, SAC, TD3, RecurrentPPO, TQC, TRPO
key_results: Best SORL reduces transformer overload from 93% to 75%; default-weighted MORL beats rule-based controller by 77% in economic cost
limitations: Abstract only; overload remains frequent; shielding not proven

authors: Manzoor T.; Lall B.; Panigrahi B.K.
problem: Voltage-aware EV charging on modified IEEE 34-bus with 150 chargers, PV and V2G ablations
method: PI-TD3 (differentiable power flow + battery dynamics)
key_results: Removing PV: +6% cost, +23% voltage violations; disabling V2G: +12% cost, +17% voltage deviation
limitations: Abstract only; ablation study of PI-TD3

authors: Rahali H.; Poddubnyy A.; Nguyen P.
problem: EV smart charging with building load and PV
method: Model-based offline RL (behavioural cloning of MPC; MPC as policy estimator) vs model-free PPO
key_results: Both approaches ~20% savings
limitations: Abstract only

authors: Diaz-Londono C.; Orfanoudakis S.; Vergara P.P.; Palensky P.; Ruiz F.; Gruosso G.
problem: G2V/V2G demand response with battery-degradation awareness
method: Open-source MPC algorithms (basis of EV2Gym eMPC/OCMF baselines)
key_results: Real-time schedules considering prices, grid constraints and user preferences (qualitative)
limitations: Abstract only; feasibility relies on forecasts within horizon

authors: Jing B.; Liu Z.; Jiang Y.; Zhu G.
problem: Community aggregator, 300 EVs under strict transformer capacity with incomplete SoC information
method: Hybrid-priority MPC with dynamic priority index and three-stage power allocation (priority guarantee, demand-based distribution, capacity filling)
environment_or_data: Simulation with dynamic base load and randomised vehicle states
key_results: No transformer overload; 96.5% completion for urgent vehicles, 99.5% overall
limitations: Not RL; departure energy not guaranteed

authors: Wang B.; Yao Y.; Gao J.; Luo D.
problem: Large-scale charging station: EV-charger matching + continuous power dispatch under charger and station-level power limits
method: SMPD: supervised matching network + SAC power dispatch
architecture: Supervised scoring network with masking of infeasible pairs; SAC (details not read)
key_results: Lower waiting time, higher revenue, comparable demand satisfaction (qualitative)
limitations: Stage II constraint mechanism not visible in what was read

authors: Baweja A.S.; Lakshmi C.
problem: Distributed resource coordination: EV charging demand balancing over 247 Shenzhen zones; cloud cost governance
method: NEXUS-MARL: heterogeneous graph transformer + learned information gate + counterfactual centralized critic
environment_or_data: ST-EVCDP dataset; Google Cluster Trace v3
key_results: 17.8% better demand equity (EV); zero-shot 200 -> 800/2,000 machines in cloud domain
limitations: Abstract only; EV task is zone-level demand balancing, no physical charging constraints

authors: Yan H.; Ding S.; Zhang J.; Yao X.; Liu Y.; Wang H.; Luo C.; Shi Y.
problem: OPF with EV charging stations at buses (IEEE 14/30, modified 141-bus); hourly V2G scheduling
method: HPC-RL: upper-level GRG-SAC enforcing AC power-balance and generator/voltage limits; lower-level dynamic boundary giving per-EV feasible power bounds for departure SoC
environment_or_data: Custom PyTorch + MATLAB CVX baselines (not EV2Gym)
key_results: 100% demand satisfaction; inequality violations 0.00; equality violation 0.0020/0.0002/0.4138; objective gap to MPC 10.2%/13.1%/7.2%
limitations: Only first-order Proposition (tangent-space feasibility); dynamic boundary claimed 'mathematically guaranteeing' without proof and without aggregate-capacity feasibility analysis; no transformer limit; no zero-shot size transfer

authors: Wan G.; Zeng P.; Dong X.; Song C.; Cui S.; Li D.; et al.
problem: Hybrid-action CPS optimisation incl. an EV charging station scenario (transformer capacity, charger current limits)
method: LIRL: policy gradient with projection of a latent action onto the logic-defined admissible set (Hungarian + convex QP via OSQP)
architecture: Fixed-size latent action decoder (trained per configuration)
key_results: EV station: zero transformer/current violations vs 24.77% (PDQN) and 57.34% (HPPO); 90.4% per-vehicle success
limitations: Lemma 1 is generic feasibility-by-construction of a QP projection assuming non-empty feasible set; departure energy not a constraint in EV case; no size transfer
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.00806 (WebFetch; EV case details in supplementary not available)

authors: Song G.; Xie H.; Zhang J.; Fu H.; Shi Z.; Feng D.; Song X.; Zhang H.
problem: Multi-station collaborative EV charging energy management
method: MAHEM: transformer-based MARL with Q-value decomposition and attention-based communication
key_results: 31.6% lower total charging cost; robustness and transfer tests mentioned
limitations: Abstract only; no constraint guarantees mentioned

authors: Zhang Z.; Rigo-Mariani R.; Hadjsaid N.; Xu Y.
problem: Grid-to-vehicle management in a distribution grid with transformer electrical and thermal limits, voltage and line limits; unknown departure times/energies
method: Projection-based Constrained Policy Optimization (PCPO), model-free
environment_or_data: Distribution grid simulation with temperature scenarios
baselines: Conventional DRL and other safe DRL
key_results: 92% energy delivered vs <80% for benchmarks; up to 90% lower transformer ageing vs uncontrolled
limitations: Abstract only; PCPO projects policy parameters (expected-cost constraint), not per-step actions
